#Web platform conformance

On this page

  • Passing subtests over time
  • Pass rate by folder
  • How this is measured
  • Reference tests

Wren runs a sample of the web-platform-tests (WPT) and records, for each subtest, the result it expects (wpt/expectations). This page shows how many subtests pass and how the number has grown, folder by folder.

Read the numbers honestly. Wren measures a handful of WPT folders, not the whole suite. The totals below are not comparable with the per-browser scores on wpt.fyi: those run the entire test suite, this runs a few thousand subtests in the folders Wren has code for. A high percentage here means "the part Wren claims to do, it does", not "Wren is as complete as another browser".

#Passing subtests over time

The curve is rebuilt from the git history of wpt/expectations: one point per commit that touches it, a subtest counting as passing when its recorded result is exactly PASS.

The purple line is every folder measured at that moment — adding a new folder adds its subtests, so the line steps up when Wren starts measuring more of the web. The blue line counts only the folders that were measured at the start, so it shows progress at a fixed scope.

#How this is measured

build\wpt.exe -update runs the tests and writes the expectations; build\wpt.exe -only <folder> runs one folder. The chart and the table on this page are generated from wpt/expectations (and build\wpt\report.md when a run has produced it) by src/tools/docsite, the same tool that builds this site. Nothing here is typed by hand, so it cannot drift from the recorded results.

Most folders run without layout: what their tests read of geometry is 0, and their expectations say so. The folders that test geometry (LAYOUT_FOLDERS in src/tools/wpt/layout_host.odin: dom/events/scrolling, css/css-anchor-position, css/css-multicol, css/css-writing-modes, css/cssom, html/semantics/interactive-elements/the-dialog-element, navigation-api/scroll-behavior) get a layout of an 800 x 600 with fixed text metrics, so that getComputedStyle, offsetTop or getBoundingClientRect answer there as a page's; the documents of their frames are laid out too, each in its container's content box. A page's autofocus runs once its scripts had their turn, as the shell runs it. A test that loads testdriver.js gets the same layout, and its input: wpt/testdriver-vendor.js (served in place of WPT's own) hands test_driver's click, send_keys, action_sequence (and bless, which clicks) to the runner, which performs them through the browser's own input path, in process (src/tools/wpt/testdriver.odin: a hit test of the layout, pointer and mouse events, the focus, the click and its activation behaviour, keys and their default actions, keyboard scrolling, wheel events and the scrolling they do, at once where the shell animates it). A mouse is the only pointer; touch and pen pointers and the other actions (cookies, permissions, another window...) fail at once instead of waiting for a person until the test's time is up, and are counted as failing.

#Reference tests

The numbers above are testharness subtests. Reference tests compare two pages pixel by pixel, and they are counted apart: never in the chart or the table above, in a table of their own in build\wpt\report.md, with expectations of their own (wpt/expectations/<folder>.reftest, one result per test: PASS, FAIL, TIMEOUT, ERROR, CRASH). They run only in the folders of REFTEST_FOLDERS (src/tools/wpt/layout_host.odin): css/css-multicol and css/css-writing-modes.

build\wpt.exe -reftests all of them
build\wpt.exe -reftests -only css/css-multicol one folder's
build\wpt.exe -reftests -only css/css-multicol -update ...and rewrite that folder's expectations
build\wpt.exe -no-reftests testharness tests only
build\wpt.exe -reftests -dump <directory> the pictures of what fails

How a test is told. As WPT's manifest does at the pinned commit: a page with <link rel=match> or rel=mismatch, not one with testharness.js (that is a testharness test), not one WPT's names make a reference (a reference folder, -ref, ref-, -notref), a print test (-print, a print folder, <meta name=reftest-pages>: there is no paged layout here) or a visual one.

What is compared. Both pages load as any test does, and are laid out on the same headless layout as the folders with geometry: a viewport of 800 x 600 (<meta name=viewport-size> is honoured), fixed text metrics. The screenshot comes after the load event and web fonts; with class=reftest-wait on the root, TestRendered is fired there and the class is waited for, within the test's time limit (TIMEOUT). Then a software rasteriser (src/tools/wpt/reftest) draws the layout's display list, with no GPU and no font engine: every pixel is sampled at its centre, through clips (rounded ones too) and transforms (3D planes too), edges of boxes snapped to whole pixels first. It draws the canvas, background colours, gradients (linear, radial, conic; interpolated in sRGB whatever the space asked for), images (the page's decoders), box shadows (a gaussian: exact for a square box, by distance to the edge for a rounded one), borders of every style, outlines, inline boxes, list markers, opacity groups and separable blend modes.

Text is the rasteriser's own, and that is the limit of what a pass says. Ahem is exact: its metrics and every glyph shape come from fonts/Ahem.ttf. Any other font is one cell per character, half an em wide, filled with a pattern derived from the code point (and from bold and italic): the same text at the same place gives the same pixels, different characters differ, a turned run differs from an upright one. So a test comparing text in other fonts says that the same characters landed in the same places, not that they would look alike in a real font. An item of vertical text (Item_Flag.Vertical) is turned a quarter turn clockwise, its upright characters are not.

What is not drawn, so that tests depending on it fail honestly or (for a mismatch) pass without saying much: filters, backdrop filters, clip paths and masks (the group composites plainly), antialiasing, non-separable blend modes, background-clip: text (the content box instead). What cannot be had headless stands in as a solid colour derived from the URL, so that both sides of a test agree only when they show the same thing: video, the document in a frame, a broken image; form controls are their box plus such a colour derived from their type and value.

Comparing follows WPT: <meta name=fuzzy> (maxDifference=a-b;totalPixels=c-d or a-b;c-d, optionally for one reference with a leading url:; a single number is that exact value) as wptrunner reads it, exact without one. Of a page's links, at least one match must hold when there are any and every mismatch must (docs/writing-tests/reftests.md at the pinned commit); a reference's own links must hold in turn. With -ReftestDump (or the environment's WPT_REFTEST_DUMP), the first comparison that failed goes to <test>.test.png, .ref.png and .diff.png in that directory, which the tool refuses inside a repository, with the display list of each page (.test.items.txt, .ref.items.txt: the quickest way to tell a layout's fault from the rasteriser's); -ReftestDumpAll adds what passes.

build\wpt.exe -reftest-folder css/css-flexbox -root <another checkout> -reftests looks at a folder that is not measured: a check of the rasteriser on code that is known to work. It records nothing unless -Update is given.
